arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Guttentag argued that the Attorney General's legal rulings are reviewable in court.
Mr. Kneedler argued that Congress granted the Attorney General final authority on legal questions.
Mr. Guttentag stated that no final deportation order exists until discretionary relief is adjudicated.
Mr. Kneedler noted that the asylum provision requires the Attorney General to establish procedures.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of judicial power over executive immigration decisions. The core dispute involves the separation of powers. It asks if courts can check the Attorney General's legal interpretations. The outcome shapes the balance between executive authority and judicial oversight. It affects the rights of non-citizens facing removal. It defines the limits of administrative finality.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the boundary between executive and judicial power. It determines whether courts can correct legal errors in deportation cases. It protects the rights of non-citizens against unchecked executive action. It clarifies the finality of administrative decisions. It shapes the future of immigration law enforcement. It impacts the independence of the judiciary.
